children: Britain's main stock indexes recovered on Thursday as a rally in global bonds ahead of a U.S. jobs report lifted risk sentiment, while firmer commodity prices provided additional support.
The blue-chip FTSE 100 index
CURRENCYCOM:UK100
closed 0.7% higher at 10,831.52 points, and the midcap FTSE 250
also gained 0.7%, rebounding from a near one-month low.
Britain's 10-year gilt yields (GB10YT=RR) eased 9.5 basis points from Wednesday's 18-year high, tracking a rally in global bonds and stocks ahead of U.S. nonfarm payrolls data on Friday.
The services sector in the UK grew for the second month in a row in August and confidence rose, a survey showed.
Rate-sensitive banks (.FTNMX301010) rose 1.4%.
Precious metal miners
led sectoral gains, rising 3.4%, tracking gains in gold and silver prices.
Healthcare stocks (.FTUB2010) advanced 0.6%, with AstraZeneca
Advertising firm WPP
rose 5.6% after a media report said its European competitor Publicis
had won the race to handle PepsiCo's media account. That boosted WPP's chances of retaining Coca-Cola outside the United States.
Reuters reported Haleon
secured better shelf space at major U.S. retailers Walmart and Target to boost its visibility. Still, shares in the Sensodyne toothpaste maker were down 2.3%.
Vodafone
rose 2.4%. The mobile operator launched its own TV service in Britain and a premium mobile offer with faster speeds.
Hilton Food Group
jumped 12.2% to hit a one-year high and was among the top gainers in the midcap index after raising its annual profit forecast.
